articleTitle: Fast efficient channel change [set-top box applications]
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: A system for enabling fast channel change response time in a set-top box while improving video compression efficiency is proposed. Additional low bitrate channel change I pictures are transmitted in the video stream, to enable frequent random access points without requiring frequent high bitrate I pictures.

articleTitle: An hardware efficient deblocking filter for H.264/AVC
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work presents an efficient VLSI architecture for the deblocking filter in H.264/AVC standard. The computing flow is reordered for easy hardware implementation. The resulting design can achieve 100 MHz with a gate count of 9.16 K when synthesized from Verilog RTL design by using UMC 0.18 /spl mu/m CMOS technology. When clocked at 82.58 MHz, our design can easily support real-time deblocking of 2K /spl times/ 1K @ 30 Hz video application; this high performance can meet high resolution real-time application requirement.

articleTitle: Real-time MPEG-4 AVC/H.264 CABAC entropy coder
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We present the real-time FPGA implementation of the CABAC (context-based adaptive binary arithmetic coding) entropy coder. CABAC is the entropy coding tool specified in the main profile of MPEG-4 AVC/H.264, the newest international standard for video compression. We design and implement the CABAC entropy encoder and decoder as an integral part of the real-time video coding system that conforms to the H.264 standard. Our goal is to achieve a real-time processing of SD (standard definition) video streams while maintaining low hardware complexity and a low power consumption level. Our design and implementation is suitable for portable consumer electronic devices such as digital mobile TV and digital camcorders.

articleTitle: Pseudo 3D image generation with simple depth models
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: A procedure for creating 3D images from existing 2D images is proposed. The proposed method is developed to fulfill the growing need for high quality generic 3D contents. The proposed method is intended to construct approximate structures to give 3D images without an explicit sense of incongruity. The depth data is generated with simple models and by warm/cool color theory. The proposed method has advantages over conventional methods in picture quality, low numerical complexity, and no need of tuning of parameters for different types of pictures. And the method can be applied for any visual devices which output or display pseudo 3D images, and pseudo 3D content creation.

articleTitle: Augmenting fast-forward and rewind for personal digital video recorders
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work describes a set of interfaces for augmenting fast-forward and rewind on consumer digital video recorders. Our method overlays a series of images sampled from the video over top of the traditional full screen accelerated playback. This sequence creates a trail that provides contextual information and highlights upcoming scene changes in the video stream. With this augmentation, consumers are more accurate at traversing to a desired location in a recorded video. This advantage is achieved by taking advantage of compressed-domain processing and adds little computational and storage overhead.

articleTitle: Profiling software API usability for consumer electronics
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: To profile an API's 'usability', we suggest easily quantified measures that can be made quickly and without deep thought. As an example, we apply the profiling to a new API, the universal home API, which is designed specifically for usability. The profiles also help to identify how the API may be 'usable' to differently skilled programmers. Profiling an API in this way involves a logical exploration from the viewpoint of the application domain, and that is beneficial as an exercise in itself.

articleTitle: Touchless input device and gesture commands
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We introduce a touchless input device and gesture commands for operating a PC that negates the need to touch it or wear input devices to use it. We use a distance sensor to capture gestures, making the device very simple. This system is practical enough to use for viewer operation, so it is applicable for not only PCs, but also audiovisual devices like TVs and HDD recorders.

articleTitle: High dynamic range compression for digital video camera using local contrast enhancement
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work presents a high dynamic range compression technique that realistically reproduces the images captured by the digital video cameras. This technique adaptively enhances the local contrast of the highlight regions without lowering the luminance of the facial areas.

articleTitle: Low-complexity standard-compatible robust and scalable video streaming over lossy/variable bandwidth networks
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We propose a robust and scalable transmission scheme based on multiple description coding (MDC). Each description is encoded using a standard video codec such as MPEG-2 or H.264. This scheme provides equal or better robustness with respect to other solutions such as forward error correction (FEC), at lower system complexity; also, it provides scalability by selectively dropping descriptions.

articleTitle: A music recommendation system
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: A music recommendation system was developed that can learn users' preferences. The system can classify a wide range of stored music using automatic music content analyses. Users can opt for music according to their mood, using such words as "bright", "exciting", "quiet", "sad" and "healing".

articleTitle: Development of T-DMB system for mobile multimedia broadcasting service
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We show the framework of the Korean terrestrial digital multimedia broadcasting (T-DMB) standard and propose the architecture of a new T-DMB system for mobile multimedia broadcasting services. We also designed and implemented a new device called the ensemble remultiplexer to verify the proposed T-DMB transmission system.

articleTitle: A multi-standard video coding accelerator based on a vector architecture
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We discuss the architecture definition and microarchitecture of a multi-standard, parametric vector accelerator for block-based video coding. Our target coding algorithms were the MPEG-2 TM5, MPEG-4 (XViD) and STM's proprietary H.264 implementation. We fully vectorized the MPEG-2 and MPEG-4 coders and partially vectorized the H.264 encoder. In the proprietary H.264 case, we targeted the inner loop of the motion estimation function. Our preliminary results demonstrate a significant complexity reduction of the order of 65%, 70% and 16% for MPEG-2, MPEG-4 and H.264 respectively. In the latter case the complexity of the inner loop of motion estimation has been reduced by 79% compared to the scalar case.

articleTitle: Geometric distortion compensation of printed images containing imperceptible watermarks
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work proposes a digital watermarking system using camera phones and high quality printed images, which contain imperceptible watermarks. The system compensates for geometric lens distortion in order to extract the imperceptible watermarks correctly from the camera-captured images.

articleTitle: Eye mouse: mouse implementation using eye tracking
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We developed the "eye mouse" as a new user interface. With this system, we can move the mouse pointer, and click icons and menus. Twenty people tested the eye mouse and the results show that it can provide a user-friendly and convenient communication interface.

articleTitle: The new architecture that realizes seamless connectivity and cooperative control for home network systems
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: The paper proposes a new architecture for home network systems. This architecture makes it possible to provide seamless integration management and cooperative control for all types of network devices (e.g. AV, CE, residential facilities). Therefore, home network systems based on this new architecture will allow users to improve their living environment.

articleTitle: A highlight scene detection and video summarization system using 'audio' feature for a personal video recorder
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: The personal video recorder such as recordable-DVD recorder, Blu-ray disc recorder and/or hard disc recorder has become popular for a large volume storage device for video/audio content data and a browsing function that would quickly provide a desired scene to the user is required as an essential part of such a large capacity recording/playback system. We propose a highlight scene detection function by using only 'audio' features and realize a browsing function for the recorder that enables completely automatic detection of sports highlights.

articleTitle: Dynamic contrast enhancement of liquid crystal displays with backlight modulation
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: One of the major problems plaguing liquid crystal displays (LCD) is the light leakage at low grey levels. This undesirable effect degrades the ability of these displays to discern and display dark scenes accurately. In this paper, we propose an architecture that will largely eliminate the effect through backlight modulation. Other benefits of backlight modulation will also be outlined and the results shown.

articleTitle: VoiceUbique/sup /spl reg// ultra-small high-quality infrared audio receiver
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: The VoiceUbique/sup /spl reg// infrared audio receiver is only 5 cm/sup 3/ in volume and it weighs 5 g because it uses a special method of voice data transmission by digital signals. It can be designed as a wireless earphone, headphone or finger ring so as to be wearable.

articleTitle: A study on the MCHO method in hard handover and soft handover between WLAN and CDMA
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We address the MCHO (mobile controlled handover) method between WLAN and CDMA communication. The MCHO method between WLAN and CDMA can be apply to both hard handover and soft handover. We implemented the MCHO method on a wireless mobile terminal between WLAN and CDMA communication. Moreover, the MCHO handover method can be employed in the sequence monitoring and sequence acquisition processes, for example, telematics and remote health care system, etc.

articleTitle: Wireless adaptive video streaming by real-time channel estimation and video transcoding
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: A system composed of an MPEG-2 video transcoder to change bitrate, frame rate and frame size and a cross layer controller gathering information from physical, MAC, driver, and RTCP layers, calculating instantaneous network throughput, to optimize real-time adaptive A/V streaming over IEEE 802.11 is presented.

articleTitle: A software approach to high-quality video format conversion
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: Video format conversion is required if the received video format mismatches the display format (spatially and/or temporally). In addition, temporal format conversion can successfully be used to eliminate movie judder (2:2 and 3:2 pull down) and generate a smooth motion portrayal. In This work, we present a novel architecture and the associated algorithms which provide high-quality video format conversion. The architecture and its representative algorithms are to a large extent based on a software approach.

articleTitle: Cross-layer WLAN measurement and link analysis for low latency error resilient wireless video transmission
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work introduces a cross-layer measurement and link analysis strategy for video transport over IEEE 802.11. Field trial measurement data is presented for streamed H.264 video over ad-hoc 802.11g links. The data is used to analyze the interactions between the physical/network/transport and application layers. The development of cross layer optimized low latency error resilient video transmission schemes is discussed.

articleTitle: Comfort noise for compressed video
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: Similar to adding a dither signal to still images to hide contouring, a dither signal may be added to decompressed video prior to display to hide video compression artifacts such as blockiness. We propose that the added "comfort noise" be temporally correlated to reduce the perceived noisiness.

articleTitle: Improving the robustness of DCT-based image watermarking against JPEG compression
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: A watermarking technique for copyright protection is introduced. It achieves a good improvement in the robustness of protected images, especially against attacks using JPEG compression. Simulation results demonstrate that the embedded watermarks can be almost fully extracted from images compressed with very high compression ratio.

articleTitle: Image quality improvement for plasma TV featuring adaptive controls in fully digitalized gray scale system
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: The work presents an improvement in plasma TV image quality. Adaptive control of the subfield configuration secures maximum peak luminance, while vision based optimization of the subfield assures gray scale performance in the whole gamut. Motion artifacts are also minimized utilizing adaptive gray scale control.

articleTitle: QoS-adjustable home gateway for IPTV service
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We propose a home gateway architecture for an IPTV service that has QoS management functionality. This home gateway contains a multicast packet classifier and a priority regenerator that can handle multiple IPTV traffics concurrently. In order to provide IPTV service with QoS in a home network, we also design an IPTV channel zapping manager that communicates coincidently with a home network QoS manager.

articleTitle: UPnP AV architectural multimedia system with a home gateway powered by the OSGi platform
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: The key issue of multimedia systems in a home network environment is interoperability among different kinds of multimedia devices. And, as for multimedia content providers outside a home, another issue of multimedia systems in the home network environment is how to provide a multimedia service from the outside of a home. We developed a UPnP AV architectural multimedia system with a home gateway powered by the OSGi platform, which gives interoperability among multimedia home devices in a home network environment, and a powerful tool for multimedia content providers to provide smarter multimedia services for users in a home.

articleTitle: Improved multi-resolution image fusion
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work describes an automatic technique able to fuse different images of the same scene, acquired at different settings, in order to obtain an enhanced single representation of the scene of interest by an improved picture fusion scheme. This allows the extending of the functionalities (depth of field, dynamic range) of medium and low cost digital cameras. When multi-scale decomposition is used on multi-focused images, magnification effects of the lens focusing system cause an incorrect estimation of all pixels in the final image. In our approach new techniques able to reduce these artifacts are introduced. The algorithm has been applied both on full RGB and on color filter array (CFA) images.

articleTitle: System on a programmable chip oriented JPEG-2000 entropy coder implementation for multimedia embedded systems
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: The JPEG-2000 standard defines an ISO/IEC standard for the compression of still images. The large variety of features of the standard makes it very attractive, but at the same time much more complex than the usual JPEG standard. Several approaches have been proposed to implement the standard efficiently, but most of them are hardware accelerators. The work presents a system on a programmable chip implementation which makes best use of both hardware capabilities and software performance on a Xilinx VirtexII-Pro platform.

articleTitle: Real-time face recognition for smart home applications
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We propose a near real-time face recognition system for consumer/embedded applications. The system is embedded in an interconnected home environment and enables intelligent servicing by automatic identification of users. It consists of four processing steps: (1) face detection by stepwise pruning, (2) model-based facial feature extraction, (3) face normalization by affine warping, and (4) face recognition by discrimination analysis. The system has been applied in daily life rooms using ordinary cameras. Under these conditions, it achieves over 95% recognition rate and 4 frames/s processing speed.

articleTitle: Automated in-camera detection of flash eye-defects
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work examines the problem of performing automatic real-time detection of flash eye defects (redeye) in the firmware of a digital camera. Several different algorithms are compared, and timing and memory requirements on several embedded architectures are presented. A discussion on advanced in-camera techniques to improve on standard algorithms is also presented.

articleTitle: High-performance arithmetic coding VLSI macro for the H.264 video compression standard
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work investigates the algorithmic complexity of arithmetic coding in the new H.264 video coding standard and proposes a coprocessor to reduce it by more than an order of magnitude. The coprocessor is based on an innovative algorithm named the MZ-coder and maintains the original coding efficiency with a multiplication-free, non-stalling, fully pipelined architecture with modest hardware requirements. The coprocessor delivers a constant throughput for both coding and decoding of 1 bit per cycle and can be attached to a controlling CPU whose ISA has been extended with arithmetic coding instructions.

articleTitle: An efficient implementation of in-loop deblocking filters for H.264 using VLIW architecture and predication
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work presents an efficient architecture to implement the in-loop deblocking filter for the H.264 video compression standard. The proposed solution is based on the implementation of a very long instruction word (VLIW) architecture, pipelined processing and predication technique.

articleTitle: An adaptive quantization using modified QP in H.264
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: An adaptive quantization scheme for the H.264 encoder is proposed In this work. We utilize the information obtained from the previously encoded image. The reconstructed error of each macroblock (MB) can be estimated from the previous frame. For the estimation of the error of the current MB, a block with the size of MB in the previous frame is chosen. Since the original and reconstructed images of the previous frame are available in the encoder, we can evaluate the tendency of reconstruction error of the current MB in advance. Then, this error is considered as the expected error of the current MB. Comparing the error of the MB with the average of overall MB, if it is larger than the average, a small step size is given for this MB, and vice versa. Experimental results show that the rate control algorithm outperforms the conventional scheme. Furthermore, the proposed algorithm is so simple that is only introduces a little computational complexity. Therefore, it can be used in real time video coding.

articleTitle: An adaptive array direction control LSI for mobile digital HDTV receivers
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work presents a multi-antenna diversity LSI that enables the mobile reception of digital HDTV. A unique algorithm of four-branch combination with three-band division method drastically improves the performance of mobile reception, especially in high-speed environments. The rate of reception is 97% field-testing result in Japan.

articleTitle: Automatic indexing of consumer image collections using person recognition techniques
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: An evaluation of person recognition technologies for use in an automatic cataloging tool for consumer image collections is presented. Prototype implementations of the automatic cataloging tool and user search tools are described. A preliminary statistical analysis of the success rate of these tools is given.

articleTitle: A rapid. prototyping framework for MPEG/H.264-enabled consumer products
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: The work presents a hardware-software API that is introduced by MPEG-4 part 9. The proposed rapid prototyping platform accelerates the development and deployment of hardware accelerated MPEG/H.264 enabled devices. This project focuses on the rapid prototyping and implementation of a system-on-chip MPEG-4 video encoder/decoder. This chip can be used as an added coprocessor to give the capabilities of video broadcasting or conferencing to available portable devices. The developed framework; on top of the rapid prototyping platform, provides a hardware layer that can host off-the-shelf ip-cores for video processing. The results of this project were proposed to the 2004 MPEG (Mohamed, T.S. and Badawy, W., ISO/IEC JTC1/SC29/WG11/m 10439, 2003; ISO/IEC JTC1/SC29/WG11/m 10824, 2004).

articleTitle: Noise reduction using variance characteristics in noisy image sequence
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: A new noise reduction algorithm using variance characteristics of noise is presented. Estimated noise power and sum of absolute difference (SAD) employed in motion estimation are used to determine temporal filter coefficients. A noise measurement scheme using the correlation between the noisy input and the noise-free image is applied for accurate estimation of noise power. Experimental results support that the proposed noise reduction method efficiently removes noise.

articleTitle: An efficient encryption scheme for MPEG video
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We propose an encryption scheme for MPEG video, which uses a permuted Huffman table to encode the input symbols, and then rotates and XORs (exclusive or) the encoded bit stream. This scheme adds very little computational overhead to the MPEG video compression process, and therefore the implementation is fast enough to meet the real-time requirement of MPEG video applications. In our analysis, it is also robust to both plaintext and ciphertext attacks. In addition, our scheme can be applied to all MPEG compression standards.

articleTitle: DSP-based multi-format video decoding engine for media adapter applications
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: There are four major components in a generic digital home framework: media center; set-top box; media adapter; portable viewer. We present a DSP-based multi-format video decoding engine for realizing the media adapter application. By choosing a powerful DSP core and designing an efficient and configurable software engine, the proposed solution is believed to possess both low-cost and high-flexibility. In our current implementation, the media adapter can decode various types of video formats, such as MPEG-1/2/4, H.264/AVC baseline, WMV 7/8/9 and DivX 3/4/5. In our simulation, videos up to SD resolution can be decoded seamlessly.

articleTitle: Moving-icon-based GUI for accessing contents at ease on mobile phones
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: An icon-based graphical user interface (GUI) for mobile phones - which displays various contents without discrimination - was developed. The icons move around on the display and change their graphics or captions when linked contents are renewed. The moving icons can be browsed at ease, and contents that may not have been noticed in a normal text-based interface may be discovered. This interface is designed as a new portal to unknown or new contents.

articleTitle: Network camera system using new home network architecture with flexible scalability
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work proposes PRORIX/spl trade/, a new architecture for a centrally managed home network system. This architecture can support a range of scalable configurations, from small-scale systems without home servers, to large-scale systems centralized on a home server. Since the PRORIX/spl trade/ makes it possible to adapt a system scale to user needs, it becomes easier for users to introduce a home network system to their home. The work presents, as an example, a network camera system using this architecture.

articleTitle: On enhancing H.264 rate control by PSNR-based frame complexity estimation
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work presents an enhancement to the frame layer buffer status-based H.264 rate control method. The enhancement is by using a PSNR-based frame complexity estimation to improve the existing mean absolute difference based (MAD-based) complexity measure. Bit allocation to each frame is not just computed by encoder buffer status but also adjusted by a combined frame complexity measure. Simulation results show that the H.264 encoder, using the proposed algorithm, can achieve better visual performance than that of the existing H.264 JVT rate control method (JVT/spl I.bar/G012).

articleTitle: Wireless home entertainment networking using IEEE 802.11e QoS WLAN
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We explore IEEE 802.11e enhanced distributed channel access (EDCA) to provide guaranteed delivery of high bit rate non-scalable high definition (HD) video and adaptive delivery of layered video to make efficient use of the remaining wireless bandwidth.

articleTitle: Content-based multi-functional video retrieval system
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work introduces a content-based multi-functional video retrieval (MFVR) system. First, it describes a hierarchical retrieval method and illustrates the system feasibility by two case-studies. Second, it presents the methodology of content analysis based on the different content semantics. Finally, the experiments show the effectiveness of MFVR in generating different summarized video.

articleTitle: Reception considerations for distributed transmission in ATSC systems
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: Distributed transmission (DTx) is a broadcast technique for ATSC digital television (DTV) systems using multiple transmitters to deliver digital television signals to consumers. It is a form of single frequency network (SFN) implementation similar to that used in other DTV transmission systems. It depends on receiver adaptive equalizers to treat multiple received signals as multipath. The interplay between receiver designs and DTx systems is examined.

articleTitle: Multi-format media player/recorder software design methodology for programmable processors with hardware accelerators
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: Programmable DSP with hardware accelerators is becoming prevalent for multi-format portable media player implementations owing to factors such as lower cost, higher quality expectations, and the flexibility demands. A unified multimedia software design methodology is presented for multithreading on such architectures.

articleTitle: A CMOS variable-gain transimpedance amplifier for infrared wireless data communications
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: A CMOS infrared wireless optical receiver front-end is presented. A stable variable-gain fully differential transimpedance feedback amplifier is designed employing a current-mode amplifier as the feedforward gain element. For a more than three times variation of the transimpedance gain, from 0.3 k/spl Omega/ to 1 k/spl Omega/, the variable-gain transimpedance amplifier achieves desirable gain-bandwidth independence.

articleTitle: Development and tests of a TV navigation system personalized with viewer's habits
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: A TV navigation system has been developed that enables a variety of viewers to enjoy TV programs in accordance with occasional mood and preferences. The system provides combined facilities of recommending programs and presenting an EPG (electronic program guide) personalized for their interests. Evaluation tests have been accomplished with actual broadcasting contents.

articleTitle: Rate control for video transmission over wireless LANs
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: Transmission of high-quality video over wireless home networks is challenging due to time-varying channel conditions. We propose a technique for video rate control that is suitable for low-delay transmission over such networks. We report simulation results using the proposed rate control technique in a bit rate reducing MPEG-2 video transcoder.

articleTitle: A robust design of inner receiver structure for OFDM systems [LMS equalizer]
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: OFDM systems are very sensitive to phase errors induced by oscillator instability. We present a pilot-based phase estimator, which is applied to a one-tap frequency domain LMS equalizer for OFDM systems. However, if the residual phase error is too large after compensating in the time domain, the LMS equalizer may not have good convergence behavior. In order to keep the LMS equalizer working normally, we utilize a pilot-based phase estimator to estimate the residual phase error and keep the LMS equalizer convergent.

articleTitle: Research and implementation of the context-aware middleware for controlling home appliances
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: Smart homes integrated with sensors, actuators, wireless networks and context-aware middleware will soon become part of our daily life. The paper describes a context-aware middleware providing an automatic home appliance control based on a user's preference. The context-aware middleware utilizes 6 basic data for learning and predicting the user's preferences in multimedia content: the pulse; body temperature; facial expression; room temperature; the time; the location. The test results show that the pattern of an individual's preferences can be effectively evaluated and predicted by adopting the proposed context model.

articleTitle: Chipset development for Digital Radio Mondiale (DRM)
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work presents a hardware intellectual property (IP) module that performs demodulation and decoding of the Digital Radio Mondiale (DRM) signal. The IP has completely been developed in SystemC, thus allowing seamless design, optimization and validation from floating-point system-level software to register transfer level hardware within the same environment.

articleTitle: Depth-image-based stereoscopic image rendering considering IDCT and anisotropic diffusion
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work considers how to transmit a set of image and depth for depth-image-based rendering and how to reduce the bit-rate required for the depth transmission by incorporating the inverse discrete cosine transform (IDCT) with anisotropic diffusion and adjusting the DCT coefficients of an 8/spl times/8 DCT block.

articleTitle: A 2K/8K mode small-area FFT processor for OFDM demodulation of DVB-T receivers
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We present a novel implementation for 2K/8K dual-mode small-area FFT for the OFDM demodulator of DVB-T receivers. Besides pipelining the FFT to reduce the area and enhance the data throughput, SDF butterfly units for radix-2 and radix-4 processing are adopted to resolve the power consumption difficulty and the P&R (place and route) problem. SRAM is used in the butterfly units to relax the auto-refreshing requirement if DRAM is used.

articleTitle: Implementation of chipset for a digital multimedia broadcasting receiver
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: A new national standard for digital multimedia broadcasting (DMB), which is fully backward compatible with the Eureka-147 system, has been developed in Korea to provide high quality digital audio, video and data broadcasting services in fixed, mobile and portable receivers. We have developed the world's first chipset for portable DMB receivers. We present a two-chip solution for the portable DMB receiver. One is a multimedia processor decoding the newest video standard, H.264, and the other is a channel processor. We describe the low-power high performance design and specification of this chipset.

articleTitle: A 0.18 /spl mu/m CMOS SoC of a front-end hardware platform for DVD-multi recorders
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work presents a 0.18 /spl mu/m CMOS system on a chip (SoC) that is a hardware platform for the front-end of DVD-multi recorders (FESOC). It has one 32 bit RISC CPU and one 16 bit DSP as well as most of the necessary components for DVD recorders, except for an analog front end (AFE) and some memories. The necessary building blocks are a partial response channel maximum likelihood detector (PRML), a servo signal processor (SERVO), write strategy controller (WSC), a data processor (DP), an AT-attachment packet interface (ATAPI), and a micro computer unit (MCU). Using a three-layered bus architecture enables this FESOC to work well with a 16 bit-wide bus at 67 MHz for 8/spl times/ DVD operation, and to be implemented with a short development time. The FESOC is fabricated in 0.18 /spl mu/m 1-poly 5-metal CMOS technology. It contains 8.4 million transistors in a 46 mm/sup 2/ die and consumes 1.4 W with a channel clock of 209.28 MHz in 8/spl times/ operation mode.

articleTitle: Quantification of the optimal video-coding complexity for cost-efficient storage
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: Advancing coding technology and the ever-increasing capacity of storage media, widens the range of applications for video recording. Depending on the storage medium and the recording time, the complexity of the coding scheme is a difficult design choice, trading-off computational resources and the storage costs. Cost-distortion curves as discussed In this work, provide a cost-effective design choice and show the relevance for a scalable system architecture.

articleTitle: Collaborative help for networked home products
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: Ordinary people already have great difficulty using the advanced features of digitally-operated household devices, and the problem is getting worse as more customization and programming features are continually being added. This usability problem cannot be solved using only the tiny displays and limited control buttons typically found on home appliances. We demonstrate how, using home networking to share a larger and more powerful display, we can provide home products with a new type of collaborative interface in which the product actively helps the user, especially with complex features that are only occasionally used.

articleTitle: Mixed reality head-mounted display
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: The mixed reality head-mounted display (MRHMD) is a video see-through head-mounted display supporting binocular vision for mixed reality applications, with customized hardware for real-time composition of video from natural scenes and rendered graphics from its supporting computer system. By incorporating this video compositor into the MRHMD, it is unnecessary for the high quality video stream to pass through the computer system. This frees up part of the processing power of the computer system for other computationally intensive tasks in a mixed reality system, and hence the overall performance of the system is improved. As a result, the user of the mixed reality system with our MRHMD experiences a shorter overall delay.

articleTitle: A wireless motion system for video gaming
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: The work presents a virtual motion control system using ultra-wideband (UWB) technology and multilateration algorithms with wearable wireless node networks. It provides full 3D input and coexists with the emerging UWB standards.

articleTitle: Embedded 3D sound movement system based on feature extraction of head-related transfer function
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: An embedded system for 3D sound movement is implemented. Based on feature extraction of HRTF (head-related transfer function), an efficient scheme for filter coefficient sharing is devised, which reduces the required memory amount by about 93% and enables sound movement at all points in 3D space. An FPGA-based prototype system is also constructed.

articleTitle: Optimization of H.264 encoder using adaptive mode decision and SIMD instructions
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work presents algorithms that optimize the baseline H.264 encoder without loss of image quality and compression ratio. We propose an adaptive mode decision algorithm to speedup complex mode decision with rate distortion optimization (RDO). Also we optimize computation-intensive modules using single instruction multiple data (SIMD) instructions. As a result, the proposed encoder is ten times faster than the JM72 reference encoder.

articleTitle: Design of a universal middleware bridge for device interoperability in heterogeneous home network middleware
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: The paper proposes the design of a software universal middleware bridge (UMB) that can be used to solve seamless interoperability problems caused by the heterogeneity of several kinds of home network middleware. The proposed UMB dynamically maps physical devices in all the different middleware domains into virtually abstracted devices in the UMB domain and enables all home devices overlaid on heterogeneous networks to be seen as virtually the same physical devices in the same middleware domain, as well as to detect and control each other.

articleTitle: Fast inter-prediction method for mobile video communications using H.264/AVC
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We propose a fast inter-prediction method to reduce the encoding complexity for the H.264/AVC coder. The proposed method determines the coding mode of the macroblock (MB) by using the characteristics of the motion compensated residual image. Experimental results show that the proposed method enables the H.264/AVC coder to be effectively adopted for mobile video communications.

articleTitle: A dual/wide band quadrature VCO with programmable LC tank for quad-band direct conversion WCDMA/WLAN receiver
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: A dual/wideband quadrature VCO is designed using TSMC 0.25 /spl mu/m CMOS process. Its programmable on-chip LC tank provides 50% and 15.7% tuning range for each operating band. The VCO successfully covers all WCDMA and WLAN frequency range, while providing moderate phase noise performance.

articleTitle: Real time transmission of MPEG2 video over 802.11a wireless LANs
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We analyze the impact of errors on streaming MPEG2 transport streams over 802.11a networks. We observed that packet size has a significant impact on packet loss rate and overall channel throughput among other issues and hence has a significant impact on streamed video quality. One other interesting result is that there appears to be a correlation between transmission packet size and the distribution of MPEG2 transport packet errors associated with I, B, and P frames. Using small transmission packets results in proportionally more lost MPEG2 transport packets associated with I-frames than when using large packets, although the overall transmission packet error rate is lower when using smaller packets. On the other hand, using larger packets results in improved throughput efficiency, which allows higher transmission rates. Therefore medium size packets of size 3-5 transport packets are a good compromise.

articleTitle: MB-OFDM UWB system with multiple antennas for high capacity transmission in wireless personal area network
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We apply the MIMO layered space-time architecture to MB-OFDM UWB system supporting streaming multimedia content and full motion video in WPAN for low cost and high performance. And also we address a channel estimation based on the time-domain windowing and its imperfectness in MB-OFDM with MIMO antenna systems.

articleTitle: Multi-threading processor architecture for wireless LAN MAC controller
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work suggests a multi-threading processor architecture for a wireless LAN MAC protocol controller. By adopting a multi-threading technique, not only can overall throughput be increased but also context switching time can be eliminated. In the wireless communication environment, wherein tiny events must be handled simultaneously, the multi-threading architecture can be effective. The proposed architecture is designed to be simple so that its design complexity is not significantly increased compared with conventional embedded processors. Thus, it can be used as a MAC layer controller, targeting mobile wireless LAN products.

articleTitle: NAMBA explorer: a participative location-based city area information sharing system
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We propose a new location-based service (LBS) concept through development of the participative location based city area information sharing system, called NAMBA explorer. The system provides a platform for sharing informal information inputted by users, so this concept differs from most existing LBS providing simple information prepared by a service provider. We found that the concept can be effective in a practical service.

articleTitle: Novel architecture for surveillance cameras with complementary metal oxide semiconductor image sensors
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work presents a novel architecture of an intelligent video surveillance camera. It is embedded with automated scene analysis and object behavior detection, so that operators can monitor more venues relying on the system that provides immediate response to suspicious events. The developed camera turns passive video data recording systems into active collaborators with security operators leaving to them only high-level decision making, while automatically carrying out all monotonous work on continuous video monitoring. When there is no alarming activity inside a restricted area the camera automatically turns back to the whole view mode.

articleTitle: Syntax-based mixing method of H.263 coded video bitstreams
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work presents a syntax-based mixing method, not using traditional transcoding methods, to remove the re-encoding process. The proposed algorithm only changes the syntax element and lossless encoded parameters, such as motion vectors, without loss of quality, at the expense of a slight increase of bitrate.

articleTitle: Improvement of response time and contrast ratio in 42-inch TFT-LCD panel for HDTV
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work concentrated on the fast response time and high contrast ratio for TFT-LCD TV panel with HDTV resolution. We propose a new 42-inch LCD TV panel (1366/spl times/768) improving response time and dynamic contrast ratio with the designed one chip ASIC. The experimental result shows that the response time of gray-to-gray is about 8ms, and the dynamic contrast ratio is more than 1200:1. These characteristics of response time and contrast ratio are more useful for HDTV TFT-LCD panel.

articleTitle: Image retrieval using local color features
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: In this study, an image indexing and retrieval approach, using local color features and a modified weighted color distortion measure, is proposed. In the proposed approach, each image is segmented into several regions by a watershed segmentation algorithm, and then the mutual relationships between connected color regions are extracted as local color features. That is, an image can be represented as a set of connected (adjacent) color regions and the mutual relationships between connected color regions. In the image retrieval stage, the similarity between a query image and a target image will contain not only direct region correspondence but also the mutual relationships between connected color regions. A modified weighted color distortion measure is proposed, in which different color elements in the YUV color space receive different weights so that the illumination variation effect is greatly reduced.

articleTitle: Robust logo embedding technique for copyright protection
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: A new logo embedding scheme that is designed for JPEG coding is presented. A parent-child structure of the DCT coefficients in a block is utilized to embed a watermark with maximum strength and minimal perceptibility. A calculation of an optimum a posteriori threshold is also presented for watermark detection.

articleTitle: A fast-start rate control mechanism for video streaming applications
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We presents a fast-start streaming mechanism that eliminates or reduces the initial start-up delay of Internet audio/video streaming applications. The presented method uses a technique that tries to fill-up the jitter compensation buffer of a streaming client at the beginning of a presentation and starts the presentation faster, hence improving user experience.

articleTitle: Bridging the interlace and progressive controversy using a progressive enhancement stream on top of the interlace stream and a new de-interlace algorithm
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: Whether to use interlaced or progressive signals for broadcast is quite controversial. New flat displays are not best served with just an interlaced signal. A new de-interlacing algorithm enables strong reductions in bitrate for a progressive enhancement stream, enabling optimum delivery for all display systems.

articleTitle: Adaptive single carrier modulation scheme for high-speed mobile computing
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We present an adaptive modulation scheme optimized for networking devices with high mobility, intended to improve power efficiency and bandwidth usage for various operating environments. We compare a number of deployment options and found a marginal improvement in power consumption and spectral utilization efficiency compared to fixed modulation.

articleTitle: Image scaling using vector planes and directional information
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We propose a novel image scaling algorithm utilized in HDTV and other digital image appliances. Vector planes and directional information are employed to interpolate data in an image modeled as a three dimensional surface. This technique provides fast image scaling that generates natural looking images and preserves edges while avoiding jagging and ringing effects - common artifacts from image enlargement.

articleTitle: A study on the wireless MIMO-UWB transceiving techniques for WPAN
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We suggest MIMO-UWB transceiving techniques for the MIMO structure including MIMO antennas using indoor channel modeling for WPAN. We propose a novel transmitter/receiver structure for the MIMO-UWB system, analyze the effects of interference caused by multi-antennas, and show the way to tackle it through simulation results according to antenna arrangement.

articleTitle: A high throughput and memory efficient EBCOT architecture for JPEG2000 in digital camera applications
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: A high throughput and memory efficient EBCOT (embedded block coding with optimised truncation) architecture for JPEG2000 in a digital camera system is proposed. According to the proposed memory efficient algorithm, three coding state variables (/spl gamma//sub p/[n], /spl sigma//sub p/[n], and /spl pi//sub p/[n]) can be calculated on the fly to eliminate the memory requirement for these three variable. Moreover, three coding passes and four samples within the stripe-column are also performed concurrently by the proposed stripe-column-based pass-parallel operations. Experimental results show that the proposed architecture has 4 times greater throughput than other architectures, and the memory size of the proposed architecture is smaller than other existing architectures.

articleTitle: A complexity aware, variable-bit-depth motion estimation
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: Demands for using different complexity level algorithms to deliver multimedia content delivery over portable devices are increasing thanks to advanced battery technology. This work describes a novel complexity aware motion estimation for H.264 based on pixel representation of different bit-depth and a simple scene change detection module. The experimental results show that with identical searching complexity, improvement on averaged PSNR is more than 0.2 dB for 4-bit representation and more than 2 dB for 1/2-bit representation as compared to the conventional bit-truncation method.

articleTitle: Reduced cost implementation of low SNR frequency estimators for satellite DVB
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: In blind carrier frequency estimation at low SNR the so-called threshold phenomenon appears. Thus, if the SNR decreases, the implementation complexity must increase to keep performance. We present a maximum-likelihood based estimator which is able to reduce the threshold 2 dB without rising implementation costs.

articleTitle: A improved video codec supporting error resilience and resource adaptation
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: Mobile phones have become essential part of modern life and continue to change the way people communicate with each other. The camera phones have become ubiquitous in the recent past and video communication services such as videophone are getting rolled out by cellular providers. This would require video compression algorithms that are resilient to transmission errors and support resource-adaptive playback. We propose a video codec that addresses the two key issues in video delivery to mobile devices: (1) error resilience; and (2) resource adaptive playback. We show that the proposed codec is simple to implement on low-resource terminals such as mobile phones and outperforms MPEG-4 coding in terms of loss tolerance.

articleTitle: Dynamic segment size adjustment for TCP performance in cellular networks
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We analyze the impact of the maximum segment size (MSS) on TCP performance in cellular networks and propose a scheme alleviating the performance drop of TCP, which adjusts the segment size dynamically.

articleTitle: CEA-2027 A User Interface for Home Networks using Web-based Protocols
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: CEA-2027 A User Interface for Home Networks Using Web-based Protocols is a new standard that uses select Internet protocols to define a common method for remote control of consumer electronics (CE) devices connected in a home network by presenting device controls to a user via a graphical user interface (GUI) on a digital television (DTV) screen or PC.

articleTitle: A unified framework of multimedia service based on SIP
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We propose a unified framework for a multimedia service, which is based on SIP as signaling protocol, to achieve significant improvements in the productivity of developing a multimedia system, and obtain trustworthiness and interoperability. A middleware platform based on our framework is designed and implemented.

articleTitle: A study on data spreading OFDM combined with space-time block codes
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: A data spreading OFDM scheme is an effective scheme to improve characteristics under multi-path fading. However, the performance of the data spreading scheme under Rayleigh fading channels is not always good. To improve this problem, transmission diversity is an effective scheme and it is possible to improve performance further by combining a coding scheme. In this work, data spreading OFDM combined with STBC (space-time block codes) is proposed. As the result of simulation shows, good improvement of performance under severe Rayleigh fading environments was confirmed.

articleTitle: The second-generation HDD car navigation system
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work presents the technology of our latest HDD car navigation system. The system includes a high performance music server, realizing quadruple speed recording/playback with music characteristics detection, a new technology of map drawing and enhanced network functions that can be used both in a car and at home.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a FFT/IFFT soft IP generator for OFDM system
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We design an automatic generation environment for a fast Fourier transform (FFT) and inverse fast Fourier transform (IFFT) hardware accelerator with various parameters. The target application is the FFT/IFFT core, from 8 to 8192 points, for OFDM systems. With different input parameters and constraints, our FFT/IFFT soft IP generator can automatically generate complete design results including the synthesizable Verilog HDL code, test bench, and synthesis script files. We also produce the on-chip-bus interface circuit, compliant with the AMBA protocol, and associated device driver so that the generated IP is ready for system-on-chip (SOC) integration. Therefore, not only reducing the time-to-market development cost, the proposed design can provide a reuseable and programmable IP core which is suitable for SoC applications.

articleTitle: Natural images classification by multiple pixel analysis
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work describes an algorithm aimed at performing an automatic natural scene image classification. It is based on a combined analysis of chromatic and spatial features of the pixels, for the recognition of landscape and portrait scenes. Quantitative results are also presented and show the effectiveness of the combined analysis proposed. Various image processing applications can easily take advantage of the proposed solution.

articleTitle: Biometrically auditable public key infrastructure technology for secure multimedia content
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: A system for signing and tracing the use of digital content based on biometrically generated key-pairs is described. The system is designed to protect the fair use rights of end-users and can be readily incorporated into networked CE appliances.

articleTitle: Flicker reduction technique in MPEG-2 video by post-processing
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: Flicker is one of the artifacts of MPEG-2 coded video caused by the display's gamma characteristics and depends on the picture texture. In order to improve the picture quality, we have developed a technique of reducing the flicker by display gamma simulations in the decoded pictures. The effectiveness was confirmed by experiments. The process is less complex, and the implementation of this technique in digital TV receivers is expected to improve the coded picture quality.

articleTitle: Masking noise in up-scaled video on large displays
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: Noise is often annoyingly visible on large flat-screen television sets, particularly if spatially up-converted standard definition material is displayed. We introduce a novel method to reduce the perceived noise that exploits noise masking.

articleTitle: Evaluating a 16-bit YCbCr (6:5:5) color representation for low memory, embedded video processing
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work examines a 16-bit YCbCr (6:5:5) color representation for limited-memory, embedded video-processing applications. The 16-bit format, combined with YCbCr 4:2:0 video streams, reduces storage requirements by 29% over a 4:2:0 chroma format and 65% over a baseline 24-bit YCbCr format while providing satisfactory image quality and sufficient information for motion estimation.

articleTitle: Personalized TV services based on TV-anytime for PDR
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We present the design and implementation of a TV-anytime compliant PDR (personal digital recorder) to provide personalized services according to user preferences and various terminal/network conditions. This paper mainly details a metadata engine which consists of metadata demultiplexing, metadata decoding, and metadata-based content browsing. The implemented PDR, employing the metadata engine, is successfully tested with a set of service scenarios in an end-to-end broadcasting test-bed.

articleTitle: A new A/V content storage format for recording interactive TV
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: Digital TV is now being enhanced with interactivity based on such standards as Multimedia Home Platform (MHP) and Digital TV Application Software Environment (DASE). Recording digital TV with interactivity poses some problems when the interactivity is directly linked to the A/V content. We analyze the issues for A/V stream format for iTV recording, and propose a new A/V content format for recording interactive TV.

articleTitle: Design of multi-standard (IEEE 802.11a/b/g and WCDMA) RF front-end using reconfigurable mixer
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We review the design method for a multi-standard RF front-end and propose a multi-standard RF front-end that uses a reconfigurable mixer with a flexible input matching network to cover the 2-6 GHz frequency band. System level design and simulation for IEEE 802.11a/b/g and WCDMA are performed using the proposed RF front-end.

articleTitle: Effective designation of specific shots on video service system utilizing Mahalanobis distance
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: A new video service system characterized by specific shot designation at high recall rate was built based on segmented motion vector magnitudes on each block of video frames, and inter-block correlations for making a decision logically. This video service system was applied to find out dramatic scenes from live video of baseball games.

articleTitle: Living furniture: life support at home by lifelike furnishings and appliances
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We propose lifelike furniture, which interacts with persons thoughtfully. Each piece of furniture supports persons by stand-alone, and they cooperate with each other to provide complex support. We implemented working prototypes of furniture and the platform for integrated services.

articleTitle: MAGIC BRUSH: a system for automatic removal and restoration of a region in digital video
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We propose the MAGIC BRUSH that is a system for automatic removal and restoration of a region based on a genetic algorithm and an anisotropic diffusion. The proposed system can be used to make a natural scene in which the commercial advertisements, subtitles or logos in digital videos are removed.

articleTitle: An XML-based single sign-on scheme supporting OSGi framework
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work propose a single sign-on scheme in which a mobile user offers his credential information to the home network working with the OSGi service platform for obtaining user authentication and accesses to another domain using this authentication, based on the SAML standard. Having a SAML artifact in the mobile device, it can overcome the handicap of the low computing and memory capability in the mobile device.

articleTitle: OTA based active current-mode resonator [active filter applications]
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work presents the design of an active current-mode resonator with complex coefficients based on the operational transconductance amplifier (OTA). The proposed active resonator can be used as a foundation to realize high-order complex filters in cascade or leapfrog configurations. For realizing the active resonator herein, only two grounded capacitors as passive elements are required. Thus, the proposed active resonator is suitable for integrated circuit realization. Simulation results are also obtained to verify the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of a smart antenna system using a novel beamforming algorithm in the CDMA2000 1X channel
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: In order to achieve the maximum gain along the desired signal, This work propose a beamforming algorithm that utilizes the generalized on-off algorithm. Also, we present a novel demodulation method enhancing the performance of the smart antenna by using the pilot channel of the CDMA2000 1X channel to obtain the exact weight vector.

articleTitle: An adaptive interpolation using spatial varying filter
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We propose an adaptive interpolation method for digital images. This new algorithm is simple and yet efficient in enlarging images. First, the edge orientation in an image is detected, and then this information is used to determine suitable weights for neighboring pixels when interpolating the current pixel. The proposed algorithm obtains better results in both subjective and objective quality measurements over existing methods.

articleTitle: Jagging artifact free interpolation [video signal processing]
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: Digital display products are gradually becoming diversified and pursuing high-quality image display. Digital TV supports various video signal formats from conventional SD to digital HD, because format conversion of the video image is required. Traditional format conversion of the video image is achieved by a 1D linear interpolator applied in both horizontal and vertical directions. Jagging artifacts can be expressed as the linkage of line segments in several directions. We present a method that removes jagging artifacts effectively using PCA (principle component analysis) and preserves the detail in a given image.

articleTitle: NTSC/PAL/SECAM digital video decoder with high-precision resamplers
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work presents an all-digital multi-standard video decoder using a single crystal oscillator of fixed frequency. Digital phase-locked loops (PLL) and fractional delay filters implement resampling of video data, which eliminates the need for analog PLL that generate clocks locked to input video.

articleTitle: New low cost algorithms for key functions in video post-processing subsystem
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: Deinterlacing, scaling, and sharpness improvement are key functions in a video post-processing subsystem. Our paper presents new low-cost algorithms for these functions, whose novelty lies in the usage of only a few line memories.

articleTitle: Embedded wireless LAN base-band processor for ubiquitous computing systems
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We propose a ubiquitous computing processor, which contains an IEEE802.11b wireless LAN for a communication channel. The IEEE802.11b wireless LAN would play an important role in the first generation of ubiquitous computing systems. In this work, the hardwired IEEE802.11b wireless LAN base-band processor, which supports the AMBA interface, was implemented and verified within a verification environment. As a result of this verification, we demonstrated that the implemented wireless baseband processor supports the IEEE802.11b standard. Also, it shows that the IEEE802.11b wireless LAN could play the role of the basic download channel in the proposed ubiquitous processor.

articleTitle: Flexible re-sampling topology for widescreen television systems
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: The multitude of video formats in television and multimedia systems requires extensive use of video scaling. For this purpose, we present a new topology for flexible sample-rate conversion with polyphase FIR filters. For any desired number of filter taps, a topology can be designed featuring up and down panoramic (or other) distortions without stalling the video data stream as has been a limitation in previous proposals. This new approach enables a flexible one-scaler implementation for all applications (e.g. video, audio, graphics).

articleTitle: Performance assessment of ATSC interactive datacasting systems
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: A testbed to study the system performance of datacasting over terrestrial ATSC DTV channels is developed. A number of new measurements, defined to suit the performance assessment of the datacasting systems, were proposed and investigated. Results obtained with these tests offer valuable information for broadcasters who intend to implement IP data broadcasting services over DTV systems.

articleTitle: A study on an ICI canceller for a narrowband ISDB-T receiver
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: An ICI canceller for a narrowband ISDB-T is proposed. As a result, bit error rate was drastically improved as compared to the case where no ICI cancellation is performed. Moreover, the proposed scheme was applied to the actually received ISDB-T signals using the hardware ISDB-T transmitter and receiver.

articleTitle: A digital HDTV receiver with home networking function and digital content storage
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work presents a digital network HDTV (high definition TV) receiver with the capability of home networking. It communicates with the network attached storage, PVR, and PC via the Ethernet. The content protection system is based on local encryption, and the content transmission system is based on NetBIOS .DTCP over IP content protection system and DLNA guideline ver1.0 system will be adopted in the near future.

articleTitle: LC TV with PVR and virtual machine
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We describe a liquid crystal TV with built-in personal video recorder and virtual machine technology, its basic architecture, features, capabilities and the process that led to its development.

articleTitle: Block-based motion estimation using the pixelwise classification of the motion compensation error
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We propose block-based motion estimation algorithms based on the pixelwise classification of the motion compensation error: (1) displaced frame difference (DFD) and (2) brightness constraint constancy term (BCCT). Block-based motion estimation has disadvantages such as unreliable motion vectors and block artifacts, especially in object boundaries. The proposed algorithms attempt to reduce artifacts in boundary blocks caused by incorrect assumption of a single rigid (translational) motion. They yield more appropriate motion vectors in boundary blocks under the assumption that there exist up to three different regions with different motions. Experimental results with several test sequences show the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms.

articleTitle: Dipole-array assisted Doppler spread compensator with diversity for mobile digital terrestrial television broadcasting receiver
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work proposes a new dipole-array assisted Doppler spread compensator with maximal ratio combining (MRC) diversity. The proposed dipole-array antenna is not only capable of compensating for performance degradation due to large Doppler spread, but also improving the bit error rate (BER) performance in multipath fading channel by making use of MRC space diversity jointly performed with the dipole-array. The proposed dipole-array can easily be put on the side window of the vehicle.

articleTitle: LSI with a host ATA data transfer control circuit added to an ATAPI circuit for the next generation optical drives
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We have developed a next generation optical disc signal processing LSI where a host ATA data transfer control circuit is added to an ATAPI circuit block built in it. The data transfer rate of 66 Mbyte/s to PC could be achieved by using this LSI and the current one.

articleTitle: An optimal recommendation system for content personalization management [DTV applications]
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work develops a new optimal program recommendation system. An IFQC (interval feature-query combination) structure is proposed for user preference modeling. Based on explicit (instant query, manual modification) and implicit (viewing behavior) feedback information, the recommendation system can learn the user's preferences adaptively and intelligently.

articleTitle: An area-effective 1-chip VSB/QAM LSI for US digital TV broadcasting
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: A single chip consisting of a 256/64 QAM demodulator, a VSB demodulator, a FEC decoder, and a QPSK demodulator is described. To reduce area, we adopted a complete shared architecture of the equalizer regarding the VSB/QAM demodulator, and accomplished the entire byte operation of MPEG frame formatting regarding the FEC decoder, which realized thirty percent reduction.

articleTitle: Block-based noise estimation using adaptive Gaussian filtering
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We propose a fast noise estimation algorithm using a Gaussian pre-filter. The coefficients of the Gaussian filter are selected according to the standard deviation of the Gaussian noise estimated from an input noisy image. The standard deviation is estimated from the difference image between the noisy input image and its filtered image.
