articleTitle: New driving method and circuits for low cost AC plasma display panel
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: A new driving method and circuit layout is proposed to reduce the cost of a plasma display panel (PDP). The proposed driving method, which uses only two electrodes in a three-electrode type AC-PDP, can reduce the cost of the driving circuits by 25%, thereby achieving a low cost AC-PDP.

articleTitle: The TOON platform: an integrated system for automating the 2D cartoon production
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work has been carried out within the framework of the so-called TOON project, supported by the French National Agency for Valorization of Research and financed by the Quadraxis company The TOON platform proposes a unified platform for automating the 2D cartoon production chain involving 2D/3D reconstruction, registration and animation capabilities.

articleTitle: Optimum DAC resolution for WMAN, WLAN and WPAN OFDM-based standards
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: The first step in the design and implementation of DAC is to analyze the characteristics of the baseband modulated signal right before digital-to-analog conversion. This is crucial in order to minimize the complexity of the DAC. The paper demonstrates the generalized derivation of the optimum DAC resolution for various wireless standards based on the analytical evaluation of the normalized power distribution, clipping noise effect, and dynamic range.

articleTitle: DTV architecture design for multimedia network environments
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: The paper proposes a novel architecture for DTV (digital TV) using middleware based on UPnP/spl trade/ (Universal Plug and Play) and DLNA (Digital Living Networking Alliance) to enable interoperability with a variety of digital CE devices supporting content of diverse formats transported over IP (Internet Protocol) and IEEE 1394. Additionally, content metadata, capability discovery, and format transcoding features are included to match device capabilities with media formats to enable rendering of content on diverse digital CE devices interacting with the DTV.

articleTitle: A DRM system for network streaming and distribution of personal digital audiovisual content
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work depicts a digital rights management (DRM) system that implements the equal payload length encryption (EPLE) mechanism for network streaming and distribution of personal digital audiovisual content. Its main functionality consists of content encryption, license distribution, license authentication, client authorization, content key transfer, content distribution, content decryption and playback.

articleTitle: Optical head and optical disk technologies for HD DVD
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: Presented here are new optical head and optical disk technologies for an HD DVD system. The former include DVD- and CD-compatible optics and a radial tilt detection method, while the latter include new "low-to-high" media and the application of HD DVD rewritable disk format specifications.

articleTitle: Correcting luminance for obliquely-projected displays
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: Projection-based products are becoming a competitive alternative for HDTV display. It is often impractical to orient a projector perpendicularly to the screen. However, oblique projection geometry is a major factor in display luminance non-uniformity. Feedback from an arbitrarily-positioned camera is used to find homography transformations between projector and screen. From this we determine the ratio of pixel areas to flatten the illumination field.

articleTitle: A platform-based de-blocking filter design with bus-interleaved architecture for H.264
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We present an ARM platform-based architecture design for the de-blocking filter in H.264. According to statistical analysis, we propose an adaptive transmission scheme to reduce the bus workload. Moreover, we develop a bus-interleaved architecture to reduce the processing latency. As compared to the state-of-the-art designs, our scheme offers 3/spl times/ to 14/spl times/ performance improvement. Furthermore, we have proved our design using an ARM emulation board.

articleTitle: A new front-end signal-processing LSI for HD DVD
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work presents a front-end LSI using 0.13 /spl mu/m-process developed for HD DVD disc drives. HD DVD is a recently proposed format for optical discs, in which a blue laser is adopted and high-density recording of over 15 GB per side is achieved. The LSI chip consists of 3 subsystems: partial response maximum likelihood (PRML) read channel subsystem, servo control subsystem and memory control subsystem. Using this LSI, we have also developed a HD DVD player and verified the performance to be sufficient for high-definition movies or other content. The ability to play back high-definition quality movies proves the basic potential of this LSI.

articleTitle: Technologies in MPEG-4 AVC FRExt for improving subjective picture quality in high-definition video compression
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work presents our new coding tools adopted by the latest MPEG-4 AVC standard, i.e., the fidelity range extensions amendment. These tools have significantly improved subjective picture quality especially for HD applications, e.g., the next-generation optical disc packaged media such as the Blu-ray disc (BD) ROM.

articleTitle: De-interlacing with motion compensation and edge-dependent interpolation in complement using judder pattern
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We propose a novel deinterlacing algorithm with motion compensation and edge-dependent interpolation (EDI) in complement using judder pattern. The algorithm overcomes the common disadvantage of losing detail information in EDI. Experimental results show its good performance and high efficiency.

articleTitle: Novel resource regulator for media-processing algorithms on programmable components [video processing]
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: Media (video) processing on programmable components offers flexibility but may require too many resources for smooth real-time operation. Furthermore, the implementation of these algorithms must be efficient and cost-effective. This can be achieved with input data-dependent processing and optimal resource utilization. Since the content-dependent resource requirements are often unknown beforehand, the available processing resources per frame are insufficient in certain cases when load changes occur. This causes irregular overloads, e.g. after a shot change. We propose a novel resource regulator to keep the load close to a specified average. This regulator takes measurements within a frame to produce an accurate resource estimate for processing the frame. We have applied it in a 3D-recursive search motion estimator and show that, even at high resource utilization, overloads due to content-dependent processing can be avoided. In addition, object and segment based regulation within a frame become possible.

articleTitle: Error-resilient MPEG-4 video communication over error-prone wireless networks
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work presents an error-resilient MPEG-4 video communication system. The system comprises an error-resilient encoder, an adaptive error-resilient transcoder, an error-resilient decoder and the PLBP encoder/decoder. It has been evaluated under a configurable network error simulator. In addition, the system integrates the error resilience tools defined in the MPEG-4 visual standard, namely; video packet structure, header extension code (HEC) and NEWPRED, as well as three proposed novel error-resilient techniques, namely; prioritized-level bitstream protection (PLBP), protected data partitioning (PDP) and restorative intra adoption (RIA). In the decoder, three error concealment techniques are implemented. They are temporal replacement, motion replacement, and predictive motion replacement. The decoder also implements an error detection mechanism that has high sensitivity to catch errors. Finally, the performance of the hybrid error-resilient system has been evaluated. The experimental results show that under error-prone networks, acceptable video quality has been successfully retained without incurring much overhead.

articleTitle: Prototype mobile phone capable of receiving and collaborating with terrestrial digital TV broadcasting
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: The prototype mobile phone reported here receives digital terrestrial TV broadcasting. The prototype fully complies with broadcast markup language and it enables the mutual linking of communications content and broadcasting content.

articleTitle: High efficiency wireless LAN for multimedia home networks
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work describes the problems of wireless LAN usage in the user's home with focus on media transmission. Results of channel measurements with respect to fading effects are presented. The resulting link data rates are analyzed. Methods for a transmitter based link adaptation are evaluated to increase the reliability of the physical data transmission.

articleTitle: Frame concealment for H.264/AVC decoders
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We propose a novel technique for H.264/AVC video decoders, to perform the concealment of a whole frame in case of loss due to network errors. The application scenario is low resolution video streaming over a packed-switched network, in which an entire coded frame can typically fit the packet size.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of M-BOK based DS-UWB system with transmit diversity
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We have designed a DS-UWB system with transmit diversity which uses M-ary biorthogonal keying modulation. Also, we introduce a new training sequence required to estimate the multi-channel state information. The proposed scheme enables efficient and reliable communication over the fading channel. A prototype transceiver system, based on the proposed system, has been developed through the TI C6416.

articleTitle: MPEG-2 transport stream multiplexer for recording
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: The paper proposes a scheduling algorithm for a MPEG-2 transport stream multiplexer (TSM) and explains its implementation using software and hardware for a personal video recorder (PVR) system. Our proposed method can be used to generate an MPEG-2 TS stream, a self-encoded stream format (SESF) transport stream and a transparent recoding format with EP/spl I.bar/map/TU/spl I.bar/map mode for BD-RE (rewritable Blu-ray disc).

articleTitle: Implementation of baseband chip for the terrestrial digital multimedia broadcasting (T-DMB) system
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: A new national standard for terrestrial digital multimedia broadcasting (T-DMB) has been announced in Korea to provide high quality digital audio, video, and data broadcasting services to fixed, mobile, and portable receivers. We have developed an FPGA/ASIC implementation for the T-DMB system. The paper describes the features and functions of the newly developed T-DMB system. We also present the design, implementation, and performance of the baseband chip for the T-DMB system. The chip was fabricated using a 0.25 /spl mu/m 1P4M CMOS process.

articleTitle: PIBOT: an adaptive and scalable appliance integration for a universal access of a home network
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We propose an agent-based personal interface (PI) system, named PIBOT, to provide a user-oriented adaptive interface which guarantees usability and accessibility. PIBOT seamlessly accepts a ten-key based voice interface for visually disabled users or a joy-stick interface for wheelchair users as a PI to access the XML-based appliance integration.

articleTitle: Low-cost and noise-robust chrominance transient improvement technique for TV video signal processing
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work presents a new technique to improve the quality of the color transient images whose bad effect is caused by limited chrominance bandwidth. Due to the fading selection circuit, the architecture can avoid high-cost digital filter computation in prior designs to achieve a low-cost and high-performance chrominance transient improvement (CTI) function.

articleTitle: Reduced complexity two-dimensional Viterbi-like detectors
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: The two-dimensional (2D) Viterbi detector (VD) is the main block responsible for the high complexity of the receiver in two-dimensional optical storage (TwoDOS) systems. We propose techniques to reduce the complexity of 2D VD at the price of tolerable performance loss.

articleTitle: Implementation of edge map guided fuzzy filtering for artifact reduction in highly compressed video
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work presents an implementation of a postfiltering algorithm for the reduction of video coding artifacts in highly compressed video, based on a fuzzy filtering approach. The implementation considers two fast methods for obtaining the filter weights, which are incorporated into a practical scheme for calculating the filter output.

articleTitle: An MPEG2/4 dual codec with sharing motion estimation
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: An MPEG2/4 dual codec algorithm has been developed, targeting consumer products with digital video storage, digital network communication and so on. By using a new method of sharing the motion estimation (ME) between MPEG2 and MPEG4, a low power and high quality MPEG4 codec algorithm has been achieved.

articleTitle: A handheld English pronunciation evaluation device
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: A handheld device for practicing English pronunciation is developed by applying speech recognition technology. This machine helps correct the intonation by showing the pitch contour and assesses the pronunciation accuracy by computing the log-posterior probability of the segmented phonemes. Not only the phoneme replacement errors but also deletion and insertion mistakes are checked. It is also possible to find out the Korean phoneme replacement errors because this algorithm employs both English and Korean phoneme sets. This handheld device is implemented using an ARM7 CPU and equips a graphic LCD.

articleTitle: Low power MPEG-4 ASP codec IP macro for high quality mobile video applications
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work presents a low power MPEG-4 ASP (advanced simple profile) codec IP macro suitable for high quality mobile video applications. By introducing a motion estimation algorithm suitable for low power applications and a field/frame mode estimation algorithm for interlaced video, this IP macro achieves higher compression efficiency and image quality than previous SP (simple profile) codec LSIs.

articleTitle: Performance of space-time block code for DS-CDMA UWB system
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We propose a DS-CDMA UWB system using STBCs with a Rake receiver. We apply STBC to the DS-CDMA UWB system with Rake receiver and show its performance. This proposed system has better performance than that of the DS-CDMA UWB system. Furthermore, by employing the Rake receiver, capable of resolving multipath components, we can reduce the effect of fading in multipath environments.

articleTitle: Three wavelength compatible pickup
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We have proposed a compatible pickup for HD DVD/DVD/CD systems, which uses a blue/red multibeam laser unit and an IR LD (infrared laser diode) chip. The optical path of the DVD system is aligned to that of HD DVD system to share one sensor. Experimental results confirm the practicality of the proposed pickup.

articleTitle: Fast method for noise level estimation and denoising [image processing example]
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work describes a novel technique for fast noise level estimation that can be used both in spatial and temporal filters to tune the filtering strength. The method has been validated by integrating it in a denoising algorithm for joint Gaussian noise reduction and defect correction in raw digital images.

articleTitle: Protecting embedded error detection arithmetic coding from eavesdroppers
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work describes a technique for generating encrypted data from embedded error detection arithmetic coding called continuous error detection (CED). The proposed technique provides secure codes while maintains the performance of CED. The resulting coding is an efficient combined codec.

articleTitle: A novel positioning system for home service robots
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: The work presents a novel positioning system for home service robots. The positioning system uses the difference of flight time between radio frequency and ultrasonic waves to estimate the distance. Especially, the proposed system employs multiple ultrasonic sensors to improve accuracy and position update rate. The experimental result of the proposed system is presented.

articleTitle: Acoustic intruder detection system for home security
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We propose a new algorithm to detect an intruder in a small room. The basic idea of the proposed method is to estimate the variation of features of the room acoustic transfer function.

articleTitle: A picture rate conversion scheme using fully motion compensated interpolation
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work proposes an adaptive interpolation method for reducing blurs, when a motion picture is displayed on flat panel monitors such as plasma and liquid crystal displays. The method uses four frames to interpolate a target frame changing the prediction mode. From experimental results, there is no gap at covered or uncovered regions in the interpolated frames.

articleTitle: Robust DTW-based recognition algorithm for hand-held consumer devices [speech recognition]
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work presents a new dynamic programming (DP)-based recognition algorithm that is quite suitable for menu-driven recognition applications with small vocabulary size (typically less than 50). In terms of computational complexity and parameter file size, the proposed algorithm shows improved results for a command recognition system with small vocabulary size than the conventional hidden Markov model (HMM)-based recognizer. In addition, the proposed algorithm shows much higher recognition accuracy compared to the conventional dynamic time warping (DTW)-based recognizer.

articleTitle: Video error concealment by the combination of spatio-temporal recovery and post-filter for H.264
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We propose an error concealment algorithm that is processed only at the decoder side without using any backchannels. Unlike other methods, which aim to minimize errors in each frame, the proposed error concealment method employs spatio-temporal error recovery and adaptive post filter technique to improve picture quality by suppressing temporal picture quality fluctuations.

articleTitle: A Java processor for mobile devices
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work presents a novel Java processor named jHISC for mobile devices, which is a RISC based processor with some object-oriented (OO) feature enhancements, and supports OO related operations in hardware directly. Compared with PicoJava II, its performance is improved greatly.

articleTitle: Channel estimation-based equalization technique for 8-VSB DTV system in multi-path channel
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: A new channel estimation-based equalization technique for 8-VSB digital television system is proposed in order to perform fast initialization of the equalizer and minimize error propagation of the channel estimation and equalization. To overcome the shortage of the training sequence in the VSB DTV signal, we proposed a new scheme using the TS-length buffer. Also, the modified-stop-and-go algorithm (MSaG) is proposed to minimize error propagation. Simulation results show the LS (least-square) algorithm is adequate in broadcasting channels and the proposed scheme can quickly initialize the equalizer, while providing receiver performance comparable to that of conventional schemes.

articleTitle: Improvement of low gray-level linearity using perceived luminance of human visual system in PDP-TV
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: A new method is proposed to enhance image quality at low gray-levels by performing error diffusion using the 9-subfield and the optimal gamma, which is estimated by analyzing the relationship between the perceived luminance and the output luminance-level of the PDP (plasma display panel) in order to enhance the linearity.

articleTitle: Solutions to eliminate non-linearity during the readout process on optical disks
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work describes methods to eliminate nonlinearity, which harms improvement in performance of consumer optical disk systems. One is the combination of adaptive write pulse control and write shift compensation for rewritable disks. The other is a new ROM disk structure to eliminate it in principle.

articleTitle: A differentiated object priority control mechanism for MPEG-4 streaming
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work proposed a differentiated object priority control (DOPC) mechanism for MPEG-4 streaming. The DOPC mechanism is based on the standard MPEG-4 DMIF architecture and combines object priority, layer adaptation, and TFRC congestion control schemes. The DOPC mechanism achieves dynamical rate control of media objects to optimize an MPEG-4 streaming transmission according to user QoS requirements. The fundamental control procedure of DOPC is to monitor the status of mobile network traffic and accordingly assign the object priorities and object properties to achieve the layer adaptation control. The adaptation mechanism of DOPC provides: (i) the quality switch control; (ii) the add/drop control for media objects; and (iii) the adaptation streaming control.

articleTitle: A perceptually perfect image resizing scheme
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: In a numerous image applications, image resizing is becoming indispensable as it impacts the bandwidth and storage requirements tremendously. The image resizing process introduces (or eliminates) many pixels to (or from) the original image. The values of such pixels and their positions must be carefully determined otherwise visible distortion and significant degradation in the quality of the image may occur. Several methods have been employed to resize images including pixel replication; linear interpolation; higher order interpolations, Bezier methods, DCT-based, wavelets and others. We introduce a new perceptually perfect image-resizing scheme that near optimally preserves edges and highly maintains the quality of homogenous regions. In this technique, the image is segmented via an efficient edge detector to produce an edge image and independent homogenous regions. The edge image is resized separately from the homogenous regions via chain coding and elaborate look-ahead-and-back tables technique. Homogenous regions are resized using a merciful adaptive region-based interpolation that exploits the characteristics of each region. At the end, the two parts are summed up to produce the desired resized image. Simulation results of numerous test images show that the proposed technique is subjectively and objectively far better than published results.

articleTitle: A de-interlacing algorithm based on texture classification
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work proposed a content adaptive de-interlacing algorithm for conversion of interlaced video to progressive video. The proposed algorithm consists of a texture analyzer that classifies the content of a frame into 4 different categories (smooth area, near horizontal edge, near vertical edge and texture area), and chooses the most suitable de-interlacing algorithm for interpolating the missing pixel.

articleTitle: Advanced DCT rate control by single step analysis
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: The work presents a robust rate control algorithm for JPEG compression, mainly used in digital cameras. The overall control is based on the statistical properties of JPEG compressed images, the relationship between the coding bit rate and the percentage of zeros among the quantized transform coefficients. It allows a good trade off between resources and precision to be obtained.

articleTitle: Multi-frame simultaneous motion estimation and segmentation
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This study proposes a new approach to jointly perform motion estimation and segmentation in the spatiotemporal domain. An energy functional that embeds the constraints of both the motion estimation and segmentation problems is minimized through the Euler-Lagrange equations yielding a set of descent equations executed via spatiotemporal level-sets representation. The resulting motion field is smooth yet boundary preserving and the motion segmentation map reflects the motion field enhancement.

articleTitle: Channel-adaptive error resilient methods for TCP-friendly rate control over wireless-to-wired packet network [video streaming applications]
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We propose two channel-adaptive error resilient methods using two feedback messages conveyed from both TCP-friendly rate control (TFRC) client and wireless access node over the wireless-to-wired network. The proposed methods are combined with TFRC to enhance end-to-end video quality and network utilization.

articleTitle: Key refreshment management for conditional access system in DTV broadcasting
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work presents a key refreshment management scheme for a conditional access system (CAS) in DTV broadcasting. The proposed scheme not only performs dynamic entitlement management securely and efficiently, but also reduces the key generation and encryption load for CAS.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of soft state and hard state protocols based on hidden Markov model for the application of mobile devices
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We analyzed the performance of a soft state protocol and a hard state protocol based on a hidden Markov model in an error prone wireless channel, and provided efficient analysis criteria for multimedia wireless applications for various mobile terminals.

articleTitle: Bandwidth sharing strategy between concurrent TCP connection in wireless mobile network
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: The work presents a mechanism that maintains a minimal and stable queue length at a bottleneck link while achieving full utilization of the link bandwidth without changing the TCP sender. Measurements were performed over a nationally deployed commercial network. With this scheme, a user can achieve fair bandwidth allocation between competing flows within mobile equipment.

articleTitle: User-oriented QoS streaming system based on multimedia differentiation
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: Multimedia services with provision of QoS streaming are the essential goal of using consumer devices over all-IP networks. Under undetermined network traffic and ambiguous user QoS requirements, a well-designed multimedia QoS system should adapt the resource reservation request according to the user QoS requirements and the network resource status. The paper proposes a user-oriented QoS streaming system (QOs and user-oriented, Qoo) to achieve user-level perceivable satisfaction based on the novel streaming and media differentiation policies. The Qoo system provides a user-oriented dynamic QoS specification and mapping (UDQSM) system to achieve QoS specification and mapping adaptively at the application layer. A user-friendly interface for QoS parameter authoring is designed in the UDQSM system. We propose a dynamic QoS queue mapping (DQ/sup 2/M) algorithm for QoS differentiation, and, to avoid the inefficient resource utilization originating from that, a popular service queue suffers congestion and the other queues are in the starvation state.

articleTitle: A cost effective color gamut mapping architecture for digital TV color reproduction enhancement
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: A cost effective color gamut mapping architecture is described. The conventional three-dimensional reduced resolution look-up table is considered and the concept of three-dimensional difference look-up table is introduced for real-time color gamut mapping. The required hardware can be greatly reduced by look-up table resolution adjustment and further reduced by the gamut mapping rule modification. The proposed hardware architecture is suitable for FPGA and ASIC implementation and can be adopted in real-time display quality enhancement purposes.

articleTitle: PAR reduction scheme for next generation wireless LAN system with multiple antennas
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work evaluates the PAR performance in a MIMO OFDM-based WLAN system using the SLM approach. The investigated SLM scheme selects the transmitted sequence with the lowest average PAR over all transmitting antennas and retrieves the side information very accurately at the expense of a slight degradation of the PAR performance. The low probability of false side information can improve the overall detection performance of the MIMO-WLAN system with erroneous side information compared to the conventional SLM approaches, respectively.

articleTitle: Bidirectional positioning system for ubiquitous computing
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work presents a bidirectional positioning system (BPS) that provides a physical location bidirectionally between mobile stations for ubiquitous computing. BPS uses a trilateration computation by the time-of-flight of an ultrasonic signal and shares the physical location of mobile stations through a main server. The performance of BPS is confirmed through benchmarking of positioning systems.

articleTitle: Background noise reduction via dual-channel scheme for speech recognition in vehicular environment
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work concerns an effective dual-channel noise reduction method to increase the performance of robust speech recognition in a vehicular environment. While various single channel methods have already been developed and dual-channel methods have been studied somewhat, their effectiveness in real environments, such as in vehicular, has not yet been formally proven in terms of achieving an acceptable performance level. Our aim is to remedy the low performance of the single and dual-channel noise reduction methods. In particular, we propose a dual-channel noise reduction method based on a high-pass filter and front-end processing, using the eigendecomposition method. Representative experiments were conducted with a real multichannel car corpus and results were compared with respect to the microphone arrangements. From the analysis and results, we show that the enhanced eigendecomposition method, combined with high-pass filter, indeed significantly improves the speech recognition performance under a dual-channel environment.

articleTitle: Effective channel adaptive video streaming for wireless network
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We present a channel adaptive video streaming method which adjusts the output video bitrate effectively for a wireless network. Experimental results show that the proposed method can not only track the available bandwidth (AB) accurately even when the AB changes abruptly, but can also provide stable video streaming during the entire transmission time.

articleTitle: An adaptive chunk algorithm based multimedia streaming system
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: An adaptive chunk algorithm is newly devised and a collaborative streaming system is designed for a smoothed multimedia streaming service under time varying traffic conditions. An LMS based prediction filter is used to compensate the effect of time varying background traffic of a wide area network. The performance of the algorithm is tested and its successful operation is verified with MPEG-2 video files.

articleTitle: Edge anti-aliasing algorithms based on morphological operators
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: In this work, four new efficient anti-aliasing algorithms are presented. Instead of operating in the entire image, these algorithms find the edge maps by using morphological edge detectors and then apply averaging filters only on the regions as indicated by these edge maps. The algorithms show a significant reduction of the aliasing artifacts, commonly known as "jaggies".

articleTitle: Low-cost video decoder with 2D2L comb filter for NTSC digital TVs
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: A low-cost video decoder for NTSC signals is present in This work. The proposed NTSC video decoder design employs a 2D2L comb filter, and a DDFS-based DCO (digital control oscillator) basing upon trigonometric quadruple angle formula in a digital PLL to track and lock the demodulation clocks. The complexity of the digital video decoder, hence, is drastically reduced.

articleTitle: Baseband signal processing for broadband direct-conversion zero-IF tuners
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: Based on the direct conversion zero-IF concept of a single-chip tuner IC for digital video broadcasting handheld (DVB-H) reception, the required signal processing in the subsequent digital baseband processor is described. Measurement results for the IQ-error correction are presented, demonstrating the received performance. The shown deliverables facilitate the choice of required parameters in order to achieve the best dynamic behaviour and noise performance.

articleTitle: Voice code verification system using competing models for user entrance authentication
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work presents a voice-code verification system for an intelligent surveillance guard robot, wherein a robot prompts for a word or phrase for user entrance authentication. This system is designed to provide the text-prompted and speaker independent verification technique where a speaker dependent model cannot be obtained and the voice code can be changed every day for security reasoning. Experimental result showed that it brought about a 40% relative improvement under noisy environments.

articleTitle: Modified cubic convolution scaler for enhancement of edge information [image scaling]
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We derive a modified version of the cubic convolution scaler for the enlargement or reduction of digital images by arbitrary scaling factors. The cubic convolution scaler is modified to enhance the edge information. While the conventional scheme is applied to uniform sampled data, the proposed scheme can be used for non-uniform sampled data.

articleTitle: An adaptive IIR pre-equalizer for terrestrial DTV transmitters
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: The work presents a novel pre-equalization method for terrestrial DTV transmitters. In the proposed pre-equalizer, an equation-error adaptive IIR filtering scheme is applied, unlike conventional pre-equalization using FIR filtering. The convergence performance, such as a residual MSE, is remarkably improved due to the pole-zero modeling property of IIR filters.

articleTitle: Object acquiring time saving scheme in data broadcasting [digital TV applications]
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work provides an object acquiring time saving scheme at the set-top box (STB) in a data broadcasting service, using a DSM-CC object carousel. The waiting time for contents after a user start depends on the transmission interval of the contents or their parsing time in the STB after receiving the broadcasted data. Therefore, we can reduce the waiting time to run contents by broadcasting them with a very short interval or parsing them with high processing power in the STB. In this instance, we propose a novel and sophisticated scheme which can run contents quickly using a pre-processor in the head-end.

articleTitle: A digital video processor which realizes 1-chip solution for consumer products
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We developed a digital video processor (DVP) which realizes a 1-chip solution for consumer products. We could develop the 1-chip solution DVP because we used SiP-SDRAM as an unified memory. DVP has 3-dimensional Y/C separation, 3-dimensional noise reduction, 3-dimensional IP converter and other major video-decoder functions. DVP can process world-wide video signals. This work presents DVP for FPD-TV. DVP uses system in a package (SiP) technology and reduces EMI, ringing noise and total cost.

articleTitle: Preferred skin color reproduction based on adaptive affine transform
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work models a preferred skin color area with an ellipse according to the average luminance of skin and proposes an effective method for skin color reproduction by introducing the affine transform between the skin color ellipse and the preferred skin color ellipse.

articleTitle: A high-speed mobile OFDM receiver LSI with an iterative noise-reduction filter to enhance channel estimation
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work presents an OFDM receiver LSI with an iterative noise-reduction filter. Experimental results show that the LSI drastically improves the mobile reception performance, especially in high-speed environments. The die is fabricated with 0.18 um CMOS process, including ADC, DAC, and PLL.

articleTitle: Hybrid equalized partial response path-feedback maximum likelihood toward higher density Blu-ray disc
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We have developed HEPR-PFML (hybrid equalized partial response path-feedback maximum likelihood) as a signal processing technology for a high density optical recording system like Blu-ray disc. This technology is not only able to decode with maximum likelihood as reproducing the higher frequency component over the cutoff of MTF (modulation transfer function), but is also able to improve timing recovery. We implemented this system on the programmable device as a read channel and made it possible to process maximum likelihood for the Blu-ray disc with stable and good performance.

articleTitle: New set-top box for interactive visual communication of home entertainment using MPEG-2 full-duplex codec LSI
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: The paper describes a new interactive visual communication set-top box for home entertainment exploiting a single-chip MPEG-2 codec LSI. The set-top box has been designed to achieve recent audio-visual compression technologies for consumer applications, especially very-low-delay and robust-error-tolerant ones dedicated to interactive visual communication. This set-top box, combined with a home television set, provides standard-TV-quality bidirectional video transmission via a commercially available FTTH-based IP broadband network.

articleTitle: Effective algorithm and its implementation for inserting MPEG-TS into ensemble in DMB transmission system
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work presents an effective algorithm for inserting MPEG-TS (MPEG-2 transport stream) into the DAB ensemble, without any bandwidth waste, in a digital multimedia broadcasting (DMB) transmission system, and introduces a DMB stream caster which is implemented by using the proposed algorithm. The implemented DMB stream caster can be connected to a commercial DAB ensemble multiplexer, and the performance of the proposed algorithm is confirmed through experimental DMB broadcasting in Korea.

articleTitle: Interference mitigation strategies for improved terrestrial DTV receiver designs
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: Due to the unprecedented use of adjacent and UHF taboo channels in the same community for terrestrial DTV broadcasting, receivers can be subject to interference largely generated internally by non-linear processes: intermodulation and cross modulation in the tuner. The paper explains why this is so and proposes ways receivers can be designed to mitigate these interference mechanisms.

articleTitle: A quantization method of direct noise shaping and level matching for the low complexity implementation of MPEG-4 AAC encoder
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work presents a new structure of MPEG-4 AAC encoder. The proposed encoder directly shapes quantization noise distribution according to the energy distribution and thereafter performs adjustment of the offset level of the noise distribution to meet the target bit rate. The direct noise shaping and the bit rate matching scheme significantly alleviate the problem of processing burden of the conventional encoder related with the precise modeling of the psychoacoustics and iteration intensive quantization.

articleTitle: Fast and high-accuracy design and implementation for home electronic weighing scale applications
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: In the area of mass production, the products are weighed using a load cell based weighing system. A load cell is an uncontrollable weighing device. Improvement in filtering increases the speed of weighing and enhances the measurement accuracy. A new algorithm and architecture is proposed as weight filter for the weighing system. We verify and implement the novel algorithm in the measuring products successfully.

articleTitle: A novel secret image transmission scheme
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: A novel secret image transmission scheme, suitable for narrow communication channels, is proposed. A set of secret images can be efficiently delivered to the receiver, via a small and meaningless data stream, by the proposed scheme. Simulation results show that the visual quality of the secret images at the receiver is quite good.

articleTitle: An adaptive carrier synchronization technique for robust 8-VSB DTV reception
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: The proposed carrier synchronization technique not only provides a robust 8-VSB DTV reception in fixed and indoor environments, but also makes it possible to watch HDTV in the portable environment. This is because the technique dramatically reduces tracking jitter and acquisition time and enlarges acquisition range by adopting a sign detector, pilot extraction filter bank, adaptive lock detector, mode selector, and loop filter bank to the conventional frequency phase locked loop (FPLL) algorithm.

articleTitle: Development of a radio and television receiver with function to assist hearing of elderly people
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: Elderly people often find that the speech of contemporary broadcasts is too fast for comfortable listening. We have developed a new radio and television receiver that enables users to reduce the speed of speech delivery while maintaining the voice pitch and quality, without overrunning the entire program time slot. Practical assessments by ordinary elderly people have confirmed its effectiveness for hearing comfort.

articleTitle: 60 GHz small mobile transceiver (SMT) with integrated IF modem for millimeter-wave over fiber communication system
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work presents 60 GHz small mobile transceiver (SMT), with integrated IF modem, for millimeter-wave over fiber communication systems. In this system, the transceiver integrates a 60 GHz transmitter, receiver, and IF modem in one module. The system has the following characteristics: high data rate (155.52 Mbps), small size (130 mm/spl times/80 mm/spl times/3 mm), and pico-cell service area for wireless LAN or road-to-vehicle communication (RVC) in the intelligent transport system (ITS).

articleTitle: ICCE 2005 opening keynote address - Digital content throughout the networked home
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: Provides an abstract of the keynote presentation and a brief professional biography of the presenter. The complete presentation was not made available for publication as part of the conference proceedings.

articleTitle: Robust data transmission using the transmitter identification sequences in ATSC DTV signals
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: A new robust data transmission technique using the transmitter identification (TxID) sequences in the digital TV (DTV) signals is proposed. The major advantage of this low data transmission system is its robustness and large coverage. The principle underlying the proposed data transmission system is presented. The modulation technique and throughput of the data transmission system is also evaluated.

articleTitle: Efficient implementation of polynomial interpolation filters for full-digital receivers
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work presents an efficient way to implement polynomial interpolation filters based on the analysis of constraints which are used for optimization. The proposed technique does not require two sub-filters in the well-known Farrow structure which leads to a very efficient interpolator. An implementation example is illustrated showing the efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A novel control method for horizontal and vertical scaler in the arbitrary resolution LCD panel
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: A scaler is widely used in modern video systems to achieve the goals of scaling images and converting various video sources to various display devices, also called format conversion. Data synchronization, line-lock and output format generation are several important issues. This paper presents a scaler engine which tackles these issues with a novel loop control method.

articleTitle: Segmentation-based adaptive spatio-temporal filtering for noise canceling and MPEG pre-processing
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: Noise reduction especially in low light level images is an important feature in consumer cameras. Existing methods to reduce such noise often degrade image quality due to an improper choice of filters. We present a high quality, low-cost noise reduction filter for enhancing low light level images. The proposed algorithm is simple, effective and computationally fast; it is suitable for low cost camcorders, digital cameras, CCTVs, and surveillance video systems.

articleTitle: Optimizing scalable video compression for efficient implementation on a VLIW media processor
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: State-of-the-art digital multimedia platforms contain a powerful VLIW processing core. To obtain ultimate performance with such platforms a media-processing algorithm should exploit all the advantages provided by the VLIW processor's architecture. This work focuses on a method of adaptating a video compression algorithm for implementation on the VLIW processor using algorithm-architecture co-design. We demonstrate the importance of our adaptation approach and show the improved efficiency of the algorithm implementation.

articleTitle: MRTB framework: a robust content-based music retrieval and browsing
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We propose new content-based music retrieval and browsing system called MRTB. New feature extraction procedures such as multi-feature clustering (MFC) and sequential forward selection (SFS) are proposed for robust and optimum performance of the music retrieval system. Using MFC and SFS, we can achieve 86% of average retrieving success rate and 0.5 /spl sim/ 0.8 sec retrieval time per each 20 s query based on top 10 ranked list rules. The user friendly graphical interface of MRTB is implemented in a thumbnail manner so the user can easily verify their retrieving results with some useful musical information.

articleTitle: The judder-free reverse pull-down using dynamic compensation
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work presents a judder-free reverse pulldown of film images. Conventional reverse pull-down methods have trouble in dealing with film images that have been edited in wrong ways, in which processed images often suffer from frame-wise or object-wise judder. The proposed judder-free pull-down method is based on dynamic compensation, which allows us to cope with images with bad editing flawlessly.

articleTitle: System architecture for a multi-media enabled mobile terminal
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: A system architecture for mobile terminals is proposed, in which the signal processing for the cellular communications channel and the associated protocol stack processing are implemented independent of the application system, which handles audio and video processing functions and the user interface. This approach enables the use of open operating systems for the application system and the integration of connectivity communications pipes into the system, while maintaining the integrity and huge investment in the protocol stack software of the cellular subsystem. High speed serial links are used to connect the processing subsystems and the video peripherals. This improves the modularity of the solution and gives the equipment manufacturers increased flexibility.

articleTitle: Low-cost silicon-germanium ICs for digital satellite outdoor units
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: Low-cost IC for consumer digital satellite outdoor units are described. The receiver IC includes a mixer and a fully integrated PLL frequency synthesizer, eliminating manual alignment. The transmitter IC is a PLL building block for satellite return channel up-converters.

articleTitle: Motion-compensated frame-rate up-conversion for H.264/AVC decoders
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We propose a technique to perform frame-rate up-conversion in baseline H.264/AVC compliant decoders. It exploits a low-complexity motion estimation algorithm, including a novel method to enhance the consistency of motion fields. The final adaptive interpolation, through median filtering, provides excellent objective and subjective visual results.

articleTitle: The performance analysis of the DS-UWB system with multiband RAKE receivers
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work analyzes the performance of a proposed multiband DS-UWB system. We take a RAKE receiver to tackle the frequency selectivity of each subband. By combining the output of every RAKE receiver with the MRC method, we get maximal signal to noise ratio. The proposed system has the advantage of low peak-to-average power ratio and shows robustness to multiuser interference and narrowband interference.

articleTitle: IEEE1394 to UPnP software bridge structure
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work presents the UPnP - IEEE1394 software bridge structure for representing legacy IEEE1394 devices to the UPnP middleware. This bridge implementation provides a UPnP based control mechanism for IEEE1394 devices and data transferring from IEEE1394 bus to IP network with formal conversion.

articleTitle: Prototype of an emotional chat system using sense of touch
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: We have developed a prototype of a chat system using the sense of touch. Depending on the power of grasping a mouse, two kinds of face marks ((/sup /spl and// /sup /spl and//), (> <)) are inputted to the chat window. We applied this prototype to a kind of electronic conferencing system, named a remote seminar support system. From the results of experiments, we find that the system is effective for transmitting tension to participants. We think this approach can be applied to various types of communication, for example, interactive TV with the excitement level of the audience.

articleTitle: Evaluation on the performance of a digital terrestrial front-end
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: The paper describes a NIM (network interface module) for digital terrestrial TV signal processing (COFDM application). Presented are the system design concepts and results obtained from bit error rate measurements. The BER degradation, depending on phase noise, AWGN, sine spurious spikes and power supply disturbances, is also discussed. We demonstrate that the presented NIM design is able to handle COFDM signals with good performance.

articleTitle: An effect of arrival time differences in space-time coded communication systems
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: One of main goals in developing next generation wireless communication systems is increasing the data rates and high reliability. A promising way to achieve this is combination of multiple-input and multiple-output signal processing with space-time coding scheme. Naguib et al. (1988), Tarokh et al. (1998), and Hammons et al. (2000) proposed several space-time code schemes, which offer higher coding and diversity gains and are suitable for broadband applications to improve the spectrum efficiency and/or reliability of wireless applications such as in-home delivery of HDTV signals for entertainment, or high-speed computer networks based on IEEE 802.11b. In their studies, it is assumed that the multiple transmitter and receiver chains are perfect and that there is no delay or phase error among channels. This assumption, however, is difficult to warrant in practice. The time difference between transmitter and propagation paths from each transmit antenna give rise to arrival time differences in each path, which increase symbol interference and degrade the performance at the mobile receiver units. Therefore, we focus our efforts on the arrival time differences and their effects on a commercially available MIMO systems. Furthermore, we propose a compensation algorithm for a Rayleigh fading model to minimize the effects of arrival time differences.

articleTitle: EBCOT-based discrete wavelet transform scheme with row-overlapped Z-scan
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: For JPEG 2000 implementation in a low-cost circuit, it is important to reduce the sizes of the internal buffers and the numbers of external memory accesses, especially for DWT related parts. We present an EBCOT-based DWT technique that can produce the DWT coefficients strictly in the same sequence as to code them in EBCOT (embedded block coding with optimized truncation). The large buffer for coefficient transfer can be removed completely. With a specific row-overlapped Z-scan pattern to carry out DWT, the sizes of the internal buffers are reduced to only 1.7% or 2.9% at the cost of memory access increase of 2.7% or 5.5% for (5,3) or (9,7) wavelet filters respectively.

articleTitle: UPnP/spl trade/1.1 - designing for performance and compatibility
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: The UPnP/spl trade/ 1.0 peer-2-peer home networking architecture is an important step towards interoperability of networked consumer devices, realizing the connected home experience. This work describes how the UPnP/spl trade/ 1.1 device architecture improves the UPnP/spl trade/ 1.0 device architecture in a backwards-compatible way, giving improved discovery and improved compatibility with referenced standards.

articleTitle: LAS-OFDMA for power line carrier communications in home networks
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: High-speed data communications appear to be very important for home networks (HN). The work presents a scheme of orthogonal frequency division multiple access (OFDMA), which is based on large area synchronous codes (LAS-codes) with an interference free window (IFW). Such a scheme is employed in power line carrier (PLC) communications to increase data throughput, system capacity and spectral efficiency in HN.

articleTitle: 1024-QAM demodulator robust to phase noise of cable STB tuners
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: The 1024-QAM demodulator we have developed for cable television networks uses a modified symbol-decision region to reduce the effects of phase noise due to set-top-box tuners. Simulation results showing good demodulation characteristics of a 1024-QAM signal under phase-noise conditions are confirmed in a field trial with a prototype demodulator and an off-the-shelf tuner.

articleTitle: Error correction of statistically unstable signals in consumer wireless networks
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: More and more consumer electronics devices are being interconnected wirelessly in private homes as well as in public spaces. While these wireless networks must use signal powers as low as possible so that they will not adversely affect human bodies, they must be reliable in noisy and physically-complex indoor environments. Consumer wireless networks therefore need to use new and better error-correction techniques. Previous error-correction techniques concerned both coding and decoding. Research in coding gave us the BCH and Reed-Solomon codes, extending the correction limitation (the number of correctable bit errors). Research in decoding explored ways of recovering more bit errors. This work proposes a new decoding method suitable for consumer wireless networks, one that can recover roughly 40% more errors than the current correction limitation.

articleTitle: PF 41-packet forwarding for seamless use of IPv6 devices behind IPv4-only NAT gateways
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work describes a PF (protocol field) 41-packet forwarding mechanism for seamless use of IPv6 devices behind IPv4-only NAT (network address translation) gateways. The PF 41-packet forwarding enables IPv6 nodes to set up symmetric end-to-end connections with other IPv6 nodes located behind an IPv4-only NAT gateway. The symmetry, meaning both outgoing as well as incoming connections are possible, is one of the most important requirements for proper functioning of peer-to-peer applications like A/V conferencing, IP telephony and multi-user gaming.

articleTitle: Improving capability of frequency synchronizer with peak phase error detector for high rate WPAN systems
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: This work presents the problem of frequency synchronization using constant amplitude zero autocorrelation (CAZAC) preamble and peak phase error detector. The proposed algorithm has a simple structure so that it is proper for the receiver in the IEEE 802.15.3 WPAN systems.

articleTitle: PTP/IP - transport layer for picture transfer protocol
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: PTP (picture transfer protocol) is a standard for connectivity of digital photography devices. We describe how PTP can be extended to work over generic TCP/IP networks. This provides a significantly more flexible applications infrastructure for networked digital photography.

articleTitle: Image registration method for consumer devices
publicationTitle: 2005 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2005. ICCE.
abstract: A projective image registration algorithm, oriented to consumer devices, is proposed. It exploits a "multi-resolution feature based method" for estimating the projective parameters through a 2D Daubechies discrete wavelet transform (DWT). The algorithm has been fully tested with real image sequences acquired by CMOS sensors and compared to other registration techniques. The obtained results highlight the accuracy of the registration parameters.
